newsitem.title: THAILAND: In Bangkok, it pays to beg.
newsitem.headline: In Bangkok, it pays to beg.

text.p: A detained Cambodian beggar shocked Thai welfare authorities after revealing that 20,000 baht ($800) found on her was all from one day's worth of begging in Bangkok.
"I was shocked when she told me that the money we found in her possession was from one day of begging," Amphol Singkhowin, an official at the Department of Social Welfare, said on Wednesday.
"I know these poor people have made Thailand their haven for begging. But I was never aware that they made that much money," Amphol said.
He estimated some 20,000 illegal Asian immigrants, mostly from Cambodia, had made Bangkok their haven for begging.
Beggars were rounded up by police and welfare authorities weekly and repatriated but inevitably some familiar faces returned to Thai cities to beg for a living, he added.
The Thai Farmers Research Centre, a private group, recently estimated that beggars make about 300 million baht annually from their profession in Thai cities.
